questions.question: Permanent settlement was a feature of_______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zamindari System.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zamindari System:-**

 
 
• **​**Permanent settlement was a feature of the **Zamindari system.**
 
• **It **was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in the year 1793.
 
• It covered India with one-fifth of the British territory, including states such as Orissa, Bengal, Varanasi, parts of Karnataka, and Bihar.
 
• With Permanent Settlement, the Izaredar system in Bengal came to an end.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahalwari System

 
 
• In the North-Western Provinces of the Bengal Presidency (most of this area is now in Uttar Pradesh), an Englishman called Holt Mackenzie devised the new system which came into effect in 1822.
 
• Under his directions, collectors went from village to village, inspecting the land, measuring the fields, and recording the customs and rights of different groups.
 
• The estimated revenue of each plot within a village was added up to calculate the revenue that each village (mahal) had to pay. This demand was to be revised periodically, not permanently fixed.
 
• The charge of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company was given to the village headman, rather than the zamindar.
 
 
 
• Ryotwari System
 
 
• In the British territories in the south, there was a similar move away from the idea of Permanent Settlement.
 
• The new system that was devised came to be known as the ryotwar (or ryotwari).
 
• It was tried on a small scale by Captain Alexander Read in some of the areas that were taken over by the Company after the wars with Tipu Sultan.
 
• Subsequently developed by Thomas Munro, this system was gradually extended all over south India.

questions.question: If any Fundamental Right of a citizen is breached, then under Article 32 of Indian Constitution he can directly go the ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• As per the **Article 32 **of the Indian Constitution, if any of the **fundamental rights of a citizen** is breached, then he can directly go to the Supreme Court of India for seeking ultimate justice.
 
• **Fundamental rights **are the basic rights and civil liberties given to common people so that all Indians can lead their lives in **harmony and peace as citizens of India**. Some of these rights include the right to speech, freedom to practice religion, religious and cultural freedom, and more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Article 165 - The Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be Advocate-General for the State.
 
• **Article 78-** of the Constitution deals with the duties of the **Prime Minister **with respect to the furnishing of information to the President.

questions.question: Which type of city administration controls transitional areas (from rural to urban)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Nagar Panchayat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nagar Panchayat **controls the **transitional areas (from rural to urban).**
 
• Each** Nagar Panchayat comprises of a committee that has a Mayor as its head and other ward members**. The functions of Nagar Panchayat is to provide essential facilities and services to the urban area, supply water to every ward, maintain records of births and deaths, and many more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Municipal council:

 
• A Municipal Council is constituted of a smaller urban area.
 
• It is the highest governing body of a municipality.
 
• Members of the council make all the major decisions affecting the municipality. This includes decisions on education, the construction of new buildings or tax levels.

Municipal corporation: 

 
• A Municipal Corporation is constituted for a larger urban area. 
 
• The urban local government which works for the development of any Metropolitan City with a population of more than one million is known as the Municipal Corporation in India.
 
• The members of the Municipal Corporation are directly elected by the people and are called Councillors.
 
• Municipal Corporations are local-level governments in India.
 
• It’s also called Mahanagar Palika, Nagar Palika, Nagar Nigam, City Corporation, etc.

questions.question: What is the function of guard cells of the stomata?

options.text: Both opening and closing of stomata
Neither opening nor closing of stomata

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Both opening and closing of stomata.**__

Stomata

 
• **Stomata are the small openings found on the leaf epidermis.**
 
• It can be found on stems and other plant parts.
 
• It can be seen **beneath the light microscope.**
 
• **Stomata structure**:
 
 
• Two guard cells surround each stoma.
 
• The kidney-shaped guards contain chloroplasts.
 
• In the stoma, there is a respiratory chamber.
 
 
 
• Guard cells are the cells which surround each stoma. They are present on the upper and lower epidermis of the leaf.
 
• Their main function is to open and close the stomata, help regulate transpiration, and protect the stomatal pore.
 
• Guard cell plays an important role in the gaseous exchange of plant leaves by opening and closing the pore through the stomata.
 
• In succulent plants, stomata open at night and close during the daytime. through open stomata.

questions.question: In April 2017, N.K. Singh Committee recommended _______ fiscal deficit target by FY23.
questions.solution:

• N.K Singh Committee also known as Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act,2003(FRBM), Review Committee.
 
• N.K Singh Committee submitted its recommendations to Government in January 2017 with the title Responsible Growth: A Debt and Fiscal Framework for 21st Century India.
 
• Fiscal Council: The committee proposed the creation of an autonomous fiscal council with a Chairman and two members appointed by the Central Government.
 
• To maintain the autonomy and independence of the fiscal council it proposed a non-renewable four-year term for Chairman and members.
 
• The role of the Fiscal Council would include:
 
 
• preparing multi-year fiscal forecasts.
 
• recommending changes to the fiscal strategy.
 
• improving the quality of fiscal data.
 
• advising the government if conditions exist to deviate from the fiscal target.
 
• advising the government to take corrective action for non-compliance with the Bill.

questions.question: On 12 April 2017, Parliament passed the HIV/AIDS (Prevention and Control) Bill, 2017. This Bill provides essential support to National AIDS control programme. It aims to achieve the target of ending this Epidemic by year ______.

__
 
• On** 12 April 2017,** Parliament passed the **HIV/AIDS (Prevention and Control) Bill, 2017.**
 
• This Bill provides essential support to the** National AIDS control programme**.
 
• It aims to achieve the target of ending this Epidemic by the **year 2030.**
 
• It is South Asia’s first national HIV law.
 
• The objective of the Act:
 
 
• Prevention and control of the spread of HIV/AIDS.
 
• Protection of the basic human rights of the people suffering from HIV/AIDS.
 
• The act penalises discrimination against protected persons and lays down provisions for the guardianship of affected minors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****AIDS-**

• **World AIDS Day** is observed on **1st December** every year all over the world to spread awareness about the disease and remember all those who lost their lives to it.
 
• The theme of World AIDS day for 2022 is **Equalize.**

questions.question: Calculate the time period (in seconds) of a sound wave of wavelength 2m travelling with a speed of 250 m/s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.008**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Frequency (f) = c/ λ = (wave speed in m/s) / (wavelength in m)

so, f = 250/2 = 125 Hz

Time period (in seconds) = 1/f = 1/125 = 0.008 seconds

The correct answer is **__Average Speed__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Average speed: The total path length traveled divided by the total time interval during which the motion has taken place is called the average speed of the particle.

Average speed ( {bar v} ) = frac{{total path length ( S )}}{{total time taken ( t )}}

 
• **Instantaneous velocity** is the velocity of an object which is in motion at a particular point in time.
 
• **Linear velocity** is the rate of change of position of an object travelling along a straight path.
 
• **Acceleration **is the increase in rate or speed.

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• The **ratio of the total distance travelled by a body to the total time taken by it is its average speed**. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.question: The average weather pattern taken over a long time, say 25 years, is called the ________ of the place.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Climate:**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The average weather pattern taken over a long time, say **25 years**, is called the **climate of the place**.
 
• Whereas, the** weather **is defined as the atmospheric condition of a place for a **short duration of time.**
 
• **Ecology** is a branch of biology that studies and deals with the relationship organisms have with their physical surroundings and also with one another.
 
• **Environment**, in general terms, is the natural world or surroundings in which all humans, plants, and animals live.
 
• A **habitat** is a natural environment or home to a plant, animal, or any other organism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Ecology-**

 
• Ecology is the **study of organisms**, the environment, and how the organisms interact with each other and their environment.
 
• It is studied at various levels, such as organism, population, community, biosphere and ecosystem.

**Environment-**

 
• **The** **place, people, things, and nature that surround any living organism are called the environment.**
 
• It is a combination of **natural** and **human-made **phenomena.

**Habitat-**​

 
• The place where organisms live is called the **habitat**.
 
• Habitat means a dwelling place (a home). The habitat provides food, water, air, shelter, and other needs to organisms.
 
• Two main types of habitats and they are further divided.
 
 
• **Terrestrial habitat**: Desert, Mountain, and Grassland
 
• **Aquatic habitat:** Ponds, Lakes, and Oceans

questions.question:

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, ________ refers to the way our text will look like.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Formatting__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In Microsoft Word, formatting refers to the way our text will look like.
 
• There are certain attributes that fall under it, such as font size, color, alignment, backgrounds, margins, and more. MS Word has got several formatting tools which let you make your text appear just like you want. 
 
• In Microsoft Word, the character formatting options include effect, underline, and font style, while the paragraph formatting option is indentation.
